steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Businesses provide goods (tangible products) and services (intangible products) to meet needs (essential) and wants (desirable but not essential). | Key Fact: Factors of production: land (natural resources), labour (human effort), capital (man-made resources), enterprise (risk-taking and organisation). | Key Fact: Opportunity cost: the benefit of the next best alternative foregone when making a decision - e.g. spending on new equipment means less available for marketing. | Key Fact: Three sectors: primary (extraction), secondary (manufacturing), tertiary (services). The UK economy is now largely tertiary (approx 80%).

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain the difference between a need and a want, giving two examples of each. | Describe the four factors of production and explain how they work together in a business. | An entrepreneur is considering leaving a secure job to start a business. Discuss the risks and rewards of this decision.
